headline: Holiday flights cost the most in 10 years

sources.title: Holiday airfares reach 10-year high as jet fuel costs spike. Here's how to save on flights. (CBS News)
When to book Thanksgiving and Christmas flights for the best deals, according to Google (CBS News)
Delta expects higher fares and strong demand through the holiday season (CNN)
Why airfares could rise even more, but airline profits won't (CNBC)

chunks.text: Flying home for the holidays costs more in the U.S. in 2026. On September 28, a travel [[booking app]] said holiday [[airfares]] had reached a [[10-year high]]. An [[average]] U.S. [[round-trip ticket]] around Thanksgiving costs 402 dollars. Prices have {{gone up}} 31 percent in a year. Christmas round trips cost 452 dollars, up 23 percent. The app blames higher [[fuel prices]]. Airlines are {{passing on}} these costs to their passengers.

verbs.wrong: To be paid in two parts
verbs.why: Rent goes up every year in big cities. The price of coffee goes up when the weather is bad for farmers. Holiday flight prices have gone up 31 percent from the same time in 2025.

verbs.correct: To make someone else pay a cost
verbs.wrong: To pay a cost over many years
verbs.why: Restaurants pass on higher food costs to their customers. When taxes rise, many stores pass on the extra cost to shoppers. Airlines are passing on higher fuel costs to their passengers.

chunks.text: Fuel is one of the biggest costs for airlines. On October 9, Delta Air Lines said its [[fuel bill]] for July to September was 60 percent higher than in the same months of 2025. Its passengers also paid about 15 percent more to fly. The airline's [[chief executive]] said [[demand]] is {{holding up}}. He does not expect fares to {{come down}}, even if fuel gets cheaper. Airlines have {{cut back}} on flights that make little money. An airline [[analyst]] says cutting flights can {{end up}} raising fares.

verbs.correct: To stay strong and not fall
verbs.wrong: To change from week to week
verbs.why: Sales of new cars hold up even when prices rise. Ticket sales at the stadium hold up well when the team wins. Delta's chief executive said demand for flights is holding up.

verbs.wrong: To be returned to the buyer
verbs.why: Fruit prices come down in the summer when farms have a lot to sell. TV prices usually come down a year after a new model arrives. Delta's chief executive does not expect fares to come down, even if fuel gets cheaper.

verbs.correct: To reduce the number of something
verbs.wrong: To move something to a later date
verbs.why: The bus company cuts back on night buses in the summer. Many stores cut back on staff after the busy season. Airlines have cut back on flights that make little money.

verbs.correct: To do something in the end
verbs.wrong: To plan to do something soon
verbs.why: People who skip breakfast often end up eating more at lunch. Shoppers often end up spending more than they plan. An airline analyst says cutting flights can end up raising fares.

chunks.text: Booking early is important. Google Flights studied five years of flight data. On October 5, it said the lowest Thanksgiving fares appear about a month before the trip. Thanksgiving is on November 26. Christmas fares are lowest about 56 days before [[departure]]. An [[economist]] at the booking app says travelers should {{lock in}} fares as early as they can. She warns people not to {{hold off}}, because she expects prices to [[spike]] in the weeks before the holidays.

verbs.correct: To fix a price so it cannot change
verbs.wrong: To pay a price a little at a time
verbs.why: Many families lock in a low price for heating oil in the summer. Some phone plans let you lock in a monthly price for two years. An economist at the booking app says travelers should lock in holiday fares as early as they can.

verbs.wrong: To book a trip for someone else
verbs.why: Many people hold off on buying a new car until prices fall. We hold off on dinner until everyone gets home. The economist warns people not to hold off, because she expects prices to spike in the weeks before the holidays.

chunks.text: The economist says it is cheaper to {{fly out}} on the Monday or Tuesday before Thanksgiving. Airports are expected to be [[crowded]] on Wednesday. Travelers should also avoid {{flying back}} on the Sunday after Thanksgiving. Flying that day can add 250 dollars to a round trip. [[Flexible]] travelers can {{shop around}} for different [[destinations]] that offer a similar trip. This can save hundreds of dollars.

verbs.correct: To leave a place on a plane
verbs.wrong: To change planes on the way
verbs.why: Most business travelers fly out early on Monday morning. My brother flies out of Chicago because the fares there are lower. The economist says it is cheaper to fly out on the Monday or Tuesday before Thanksgiving.

verbs.correct: To return home on a plane
verbs.wrong: To wait at the airport for a seat
verbs.why: Many students fly back home after their final exams. We usually fly back from Florida on a Saturday. Travelers should avoid flying back on the Sunday after Thanksgiving.

verbs.correct: To compare prices before you buy
verbs.wrong: To change your trip to a cheaper week
verbs.why: Smart buyers shop around before they choose a new phone. My aunt shops around for the best price on a new couch. Flexible travelers can shop around for different destinations that offer a similar trip.

mainIdea.s: Holiday flights in the U.S. cost more than at any time in a decade because fuel is expensive. Experts expect fares to stay high, so they tell people to book early and avoid busy days.
mainIdea.why: Holiday airfares are at a 10-year high because of higher fuel prices. Fares are not expected to come down, so experts say travelers should lock in fares early.

mainIdea.s: Ticket prices for Thanksgiving and Christmas trips have climbed sharply, but airlines say they will soon fall again. Travel experts suggest waiting until November for the cheapest seats.
mainIdea.why: Close, but Delta's chief executive does not expect fares to come down. An economist warns travelers not to hold off, because prices may spike in the weeks before the holidays.

mainIdea.s: Several major U.S. airlines plan to add hundreds of new routes to warm places for the winter season. A new report says tickets for these trips are cheaper than they were ten years ago.
mainIdea.why: This story is about holiday fares reaching a 10-year high. Prices have gone up because of higher fuel prices, and many airlines have cut back on flights.

lines.text: Are you flying home for Thanksgiving?
I want to, but I got [[sticker shock]] when I saw the fares.
You're not alone. Holiday fares have {{gone up}} about 31 percent in a year.
Mostly higher fuel prices. Airlines are {{passing on}} the extra cost to us.
Will prices {{come down}} if I wait a few weeks?
Probably not. Delta's boss says demand is {{holding up}}, so he doesn't expect cheaper fares.
So people keep buying tickets, even when they cost [[an arm and a leg]].
Right. And airlines have {{cut back}} on some flights, so there are fewer seats.
Then I should {{lock in}} a fare soon.
Yes, don't {{hold off}}. Google says about a month before the trip is the [[sweet spot]] for Thanksgiving tickets.
[[The early bird gets the worm]], I guess.
Also, try to {{fly out}} on Monday or Tuesday. You'll [[beat the rush]] on Wednesday.
And what about the trip home?
Don't {{fly back}} on Sunday. It can cost 250 dollars more.
Maybe I'll just {{shop around}} and go somewhere warm instead.
